title: Energy Sources — Nuclear Fusion and Beyond
data_note: Specific-energy values from nuclear and particle physics references, separated from reactor-system performance. NIF gain is target gain, not wall-plug gain, and specific energy alone does not establish suitability for propulsion or metric engineering.

statistics.context: Baseline: stoichiometric H2-O2 propellant mixture (~13.4 MJ/kg LHV, ~15.9 MJ/kg HHV per kg of mixture). Some chemical reactions (e.g., Be-O2, Li-F2) exceed this per kg of reactants.
statistics.verification_note: Standard thermochemical value; widely reproduced in literature

statistics.context: Approximately 6 × 10⁶ times chemical combustion energy density. Basis of commercial nuclear fission power.
statistics.verification_note: Cross-referenced with IAEA Nuclear Data Services

statistics.context: Approximately 2.4 × 10^7 times the listed hydrogen-oxygen value. D-T is the most experimentally accessible high-yield fusion reaction, not the highest-specific-energy known process; the same file lists matter-antimatter annihilation at 9e16 J/kg. Reactor gain, efficiency, breeding, shielding, mass, and heat rejection determine usable system performance.
statistics.verification_note: Specific energy calculated from the measured D-T reaction Q-value (17.589 MeV) and combined reactant mass (5.030 u), giving 3.37e14 J/kg. NIF ignition verifies target gain in an inertial-confinement experiment, not a compact power plant.

statistics.context: Eliminates tritium supply bottleneck but requires ~10× higher plasma temperature (~10⁹ K vs ~10⁸ K).

The primary p-B11 branch produces three alpha particles and 8.7 MeV, allowing a possible direct-conversion route. Secondary reactions and impurities still produce a residual neutron field. Reactor-relevant temperatures are of order 1e9 K and ignition remains undemonstrated.
statistics.verification_note: Primary reaction Q-value and products are established. 'Aneutronic' describes the dominant branch and must not be interpreted as zero neutron production in a reactor plasma.

statistics.context: Theoretical maximum for mass-to-energy conversion. Per kg of total annihilated mass (matter + antimatter); equivalent to ~1.8 × 10^17 J per kg of antimatter carried. In proton–antiproton annihilation a large fraction is carried away by neutrinos and is not usable. Antimatter production rate globally is ~nanograms/year.

statistics.metric: DT fusion reaction energy per event
statistics.context: 3.5 MeV to alpha particle, 14.1 MeV to neutron (80% of energy carried by neutron).
statistics.verification_note: Extensively measured in nuclear physics experiments

statistics.context: First scientific breakeven: 2.05 MJ laser input → 3.15 MJ fusion output. Wall-plug gain still far below 1 (~300 MJ electrical input).
statistics.verification_note: LLNL official announcement; independently confirmed by DOE

statistics.context: 2.08 MJ laser input produced 8.6 MJ fusion output on April 7, 2025, for target gain 4.13. LLNL reported eleven ignition experiments through June 20, 2026; this shot remains the record listed on its ignition page. Wall-plug gain remains far below unity.
statistics.verification_note: Checked against LLNL's official ignition achievements page on 2026-08-02. Target gain must not be described as facility or electric breakeven.

statistics.context: ~300 MJ electrical → ~2 MJ laser delivered to target. Wall-plug efficiency ~0.7%.

source.name: Oceanographic data (1 in 6420 hydrogen atoms is deuterium)

statistics.context: Deuterium is abundant: 1 in every 6,420 hydrogen atoms in ocean water (D/H ≈ 156 ppm), i.e. ~34 g of deuterium per m³ of seawater; consistent with the ~4.6e13 t ocean total in s04-012.
statistics.verification_note: IAEA isotope hydrology data; standard oceanographic measurement

source.name: Derived from ocean volume and deuterium concentration

statistics.context: Enough to power DD fusion for billions of years at current global energy consumption rates.
statistics.verification_note: Calculated from ocean volume (~1.335 × 10⁹ km³) and deuterium concentration

statistics.metric: Global tritium production from CANDU reactors
statistics.context: Tritium supply bottleneck is a key limitation for DT fusion. Half-life of 12.3 years further constrains stockpiling.
statistics.verification_note: Estimated from published CANDU heavy water reactor data; exact figures vary by source

statistics.context: Radioactive decay: ³H → ³He + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ. Constrains tritium stockpiling for DT fusion.
Naive QFT calculation with a Planck-scale cutoff; roughly 1e123 times the observed dark-energy density (~6e-10 J/m³). The commonly quoted ~1e120 depends on the cutoff convention.
statistics.verification_note: Theoretical calculation; the discrepancy with observation is itself well-verified

statistics.context: One of the deepest unsolved problems in physics. Ratio of theoretical vacuum energy to observed dark energy. The commonly quoted ~1e120 depends on the cutoff convention; a Planck-scale cutoff (~4.6e113 J/m³, s04-015) compared with the observed dark-energy density (~6e-10 J/m³) gives roughly 1e123.
statistics.verification_note: Well-characterized discrepancy; independently confirmed by multiple analyses
